tier2SourcesAttempted.note: Japanese Cabinet approved APPI amendment bill 2026-04-07; submitted to Diet. Key changes: consent exemption for statistical processing / AI training, children-under-16 parental consent, risk-based framework. Effective: enactment expected ~2026 Q3–Q4; operative date for businesses ~2028. No immediate CMP code change required.

National Assembly passed PIPA amendment 2026-02-12; signed 2026-03-10; effective 2026-09-11. Changes: 10% turnover fine ceiling, CEO accountability, CPO board approval, ISMS-P mandatory from 2027-07-01. No new cookie/consent mechanism. Classified LOW — governance uplift only, no banner or consent-signal change required.

OAIC published exposure draft Children's Online Privacy Code 2026-03-31; consultation open until 2026-06-05; final Code must register by 2026-12-10; commencement date TBD (likely 2027). Pre-final. Children's data / targeted advertising prohibition for under-15s. Classified LOW — pre-effective >180 days.

tier2SourcesAttempted.source: EU Commission Digital Omnibus — GDPR Art. 88a/88b (commission.europa.eu / EUR-Lex)
tier2SourcesAttempted.note: Digital Omnibus published 2025-11-19 by Commission. Art. 88a (cookie rules into GDPR) and Art. 88b (browser consent signals) still at early Council/Parliament stage — no general approach adopted on the GDPR/ePrivacy portions as of 2026-05-15. The AI Omnibus portion reached provisional trilogue agreement 2026-05-07 but that is separate. Art. 88a applies 6 months after entry into force; earliest realistic operative date ~late 2027. Classified LOW.

ANPD became formally independent via Law 15.352/2026 (February 2026). Enforcement priorities for 2026-27 explicitly target advertising/profiling. Existing ANPD cookie guidance (October 2022) unchanged. Independence increases enforcement credibility and speed. Classified LOW — no new rule; increased enforcement capacity is an awareness item.

2026-02-02: PDPC announced NRIC authentication ban by 2026-12-31 (not cookies/consent relevant). Data portability obligation not yet in force. No new cookie/consent rulemaking in period. No qualifying change.

Active enforcement in 2025-2026 (THB 21.5M fines Aug 2025; iris-scan operator ordered to halt Nov 2025). No new cookie-specific regulation or guidance published in scan window. Enforcement awareness item. No qualifying change.
UAE PDPL enacted 2021; implementing regulations stable. No new guidance or enforcement action on cookies/consent in scan window. No qualifying change.

SDAIA issued 48 enforcement decisions confirming PDPL violations as of January 2026; Clyde & Co confirmed enforcement is live. No new cookie-specific guidance published; enforcement of existing PDPL framework escalating. Classified LOW — awareness item; confirms existing CMP configuration for KSA is materially correct.

Bill C-27 (federal CPPA) died with prorogation January 2025; replacement not yet introduced as of May 2026. Quebec Law 25 fully in force; no new CAI enforcement actions on cookies in scan window. No qualifying change.

Measures for Certification of Cross-Border Transfer of Personal Information effective 2026-01-01 (covers data-transfer certification pathway, not cookies directly). Cookie consent obligations under PIPL unchanged. No qualifying change for CMP layer.
No new cookie/consent guidance or enforcement action in scan window. No qualifying change.

Consent Manager framework (Rule 4) effective November 2026 — already in baseline as HIGH. Government expected to operationalise the framework June–August 2026. No new MeitY notification in scan window beyond what is in baseline. Baseline item; no new alert required.

Final Storage and Access Technologies guidance published 2026-04-29. This was a candidate-rejected item in the 2026-05-09 Tier 1 scan (outside 7-day daily-scan window). Picked up in this Tier 2 weekly run. Written up as alert RW-2026-05-15-01 (MEDIUM).

alertsWritten.instrument: Binding DPA guidance — ICO Final Storage and Access Technologies (SAT) Guidance (published 2026-04-29)
alertsWritten.reasonForAlert: Binding ICO guidance replacing entire UK cookies guidance; expands SAT taxonomy to tracking pixels/fingerprinting/web storage; codifies 5 DUAA-exempt categories; new mixed-purpose restriction sub-chapter. Requires UK ruleset, classification ML, and banner updates. Severity MEDIUM: configuration/content change; not code-breaking; no hard enforcement deadline beyond immediate.
